headline: Attackers worked the consoles administrators trust—ConnectWise ScreenConnect, N-able N-central, and tens of thousands of GitHub repositories—on the same day Europol and police in nine countries seized the servers behind Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers reach customers through the consoles that manage them, with ConnectWise disabling five ScreenConnect extensions after rogue remote-access clients landed on 288 endpoints and N-able fielding exploits that work on servers it already patched.

topics.title: ScreenConnect and N-central Attacks Reach Customer Endpoints
topics.latest_developments: N-able opened a second investigation on November 12, 2026 into a fresh public disclosure of more flaws in on-premises N-central 2026.4.1 HF2, the already-hotfixed release, with exploits that claim root remote code execution and Windows SYSTEM access, and the company says the server issue depends on a non-default configuration in which an administrator turns the Legacy API on and exposes it to the public internet; ConnectWise disabled five third-party ScreenConnect extensions in partner environments after attackers exploited a flaw in one legitimate extension to walk past ScreenConnect authentication and push rogue remote-access clients onto at least 288 endpoints across 48 organizations, and the company sees no compromise of its own infrastructure and no vulnerability in ScreenConnect itself.
topics.summary: Both products are remote monitoring and management platforms that managed service providers use to administer client machines, which gives one compromised instance reach into every customer it serves. Administrators should apply N-able's hotfixes, take the Legacy API off the internet, check which ScreenConnect extensions their environment loads, and hunt for unexpected remote-access clients on managed endpoints.

sources.title: New N-central Exploits Work Against Patched Servers, Enable Root RCE and Windows SYSTEM Access
Hackers Target N-central Zero-Days as N-able Rushes Patches
ScreenConnect Attacks Target at Least 288 Endpoints Across 48 Organizations With Rogue Clients
Active ScreenConnect attacks breach MSPs, impact dozens of organizations

topics.title: HTTP/2 and Pre-Auth Flaws Hit Core Server Software
topics.latest_developments: PTC patched CVE-2026-126325, an improper input validation and untrusted deserialization flaw rated 9.2 in its Windchill and FlexPLM product lifecycle management software that hands an attacker remote code execution; the Apache Software Foundation fixed CVE-2026-119618, a critical remote code execution flaw in the mod_http2 module that affects Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 through 2.4.70, in version 2.4.71 on November 11, 2026, and Red Hat, which ships the server with Red Hat Enterprise Linux, says only hosts with HTTP/2 enabled face exposure; Node.js closed 16 flaws in versions 22.23.5, 24.22.3, and 26.13.1, two of them in built-in HTTP/2 support that let an unauthenticated client crash a 24.x or 26.x server or pull back pieces of server memory holding other connections' responses; MongoDB patched CVE-2026-118383, which lets an unauthenticated attacker send two requests that crash a lagging replica set member once it takes over as primary; and Red Hat patched a critical Quay flaw that lets attackers steal private container images, overwrite repositories, and hold persistent access.
topics.summary: These are the web servers, runtimes, databases, registries, and engineering platforms sitting under most enterprise applications, and three of the flaws need no credentials at all. Inventory internet-facing Apache and Node.js hosts with HTTP/2 turned on, patch to 2.4.71 and the fixed Node.js lines, and update Windchill, FlexPLM, MongoDB replica set members, and Quay registries.

sources.title: Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code Remotely
Node.js Fixes 16 Flaws, Including HTTP/2 Bugs That Crash Servers and Leak Other Connections' Data

topics.title: Windows Updates Stumble as Browsers Patch 180 Flaws
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft confirmed on November 12, 2026 that the November 2026 security updates fail to install on Windows 11 machines carrying the October preview update, throwing 0x80070306, 0x800f0989, and 0x800f0993 errors, and separately confirmed that Windows updates shipped since the October 2026 Patch Tuesday degrade SQL Server performance and stability; Google released Chrome 157 with 83 fixes and Mozilla released Firefox 160 with 99; and Google Cloud told customers running virtual machines on AMD Turin processors to patch the guest operating system and stop and start each instance to close three side-channel flaws that let code sharing a processor core infer data from other processes or the kernel inside the same virtual machine.
topics.summary: The largest patch month on record now carries its own failures, which leaves Windows 11 fleets unpatched and SQL Server instances slow. Sequence the October preview update out of the way before deploying November's, benchmark SQL Server hosts, roll Chrome 157 and Firefox 160, and schedule the stop-and-start that AMD Turin guests need.

sources.title: Microsoft confirms Windows security updates installation issues
Microsoft: Recent Windows updates cause SQL Server performance issues
Chrome, Firefox Updates Patch Over 180 Vulnerabilities

topics.title: Stolen GitHub Accounts Seed a Secret Stealer
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek put the reach of the wfx-loot campaign at roughly 60,000 GitHub repositories, extending Aikido Security's account of an attacker who holds stolen credentials for 4,837 GitHub accounts, pushed a credential-stealing payload into tens of thousands of repositories starting Tuesday, November 10, 2026, and ran it in at least 1,806 of them, shipping GitHub Actions secrets and cloud credentials back out; the compromised accounts also opened probe pull requests across the repositories they could write to.
topics.summary: GitHub Actions workflows carry the secrets that reach cloud accounts, container registries, and production systems, so every secret the malware touched counts as burned. Anyone whose repositories accepted commits or workflow runs since November 10, 2026 should rotate Actions secrets and cloud credentials, revoke tokens, and audit recent pull requests and commit authors.

sources.title: Check your GitHub repos: A secret stealer hit tens of thousands of them
Attacker Used 4,837 Hijacked GitHub Accounts to Run a CI Secret Stealer in 1,806+ Repositories
Attacker Targets 60,000 GitHub Repositories in Credential Theft Campaign

topics.title: AI Agents Enter State Espionage Campaigns
topics.latest_developments: Researchers reported on November 12, 2026 that suspected Kazakhstan-linked hackers ran an AI agent to spy on Central Asian governments, steal sensitive documents, and work their way into critical infrastructure networks; Dark Reading detailed a Chinese Communist Party big data project that scrapes open information to profile people abroad and scout recruits inside Taiwan's chip industry; and Romania's intelligence service said it halted a cyber-espionage campaign by Russian state-linked hackers against government email accounts before the group moved data out.
topics.summary: Agentic tooling compresses the reconnaissance, document theft, and lateral movement of an espionage operation into machine-speed work, and the targets are foreign ministries, government mail systems, and semiconductor staff. Government and chip-sector organizations should audit mailbox access, watch for agent-driven traffic patterns, and brief employees who face recruitment approaches.

topics.title: GSocket Keeps Linux Servers Owned After Patching
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft Threat Intelligence documented multiple threat actors planting GSocket, a legitimate open-source remote access tool, on compromised Linux servers to hold encrypted command and control after the victim patches the vulnerability that let the attacker in, and published detection, investigation, and remediation steps; the threat intelligence company Flare reported separately that underground forums now trade eBPF rootkit source code, tutorials, and exploits that hide activity on Linux without loading a kernel module.
topics.summary: Patching an exploited flaw closes the door the attacker used and leaves the attacker inside, because GSocket rides outbound encrypted connections that look like administrative traffic. After any Linux server compromise, hunt for GSocket processes, unexpected cron and systemd persistence, and eBPF programs loaded outside your own tooling.

sources.title: The global socket: how threat actors are weaponizing GSocket for stealthy C2
Hackers plant GSocket on Linux servers for persistent access
eBPF Rootkits: Why Underground Actors Are Taking Notice

topics.title: Apify Rotates Tokens as Notion Counts Fireworks Damage
topics.latest_developments: Apify, the web scraping and automation platform, rotated critical internal secrets, revoked some third-party OAuth connections, and prompted customers to reset two-factor authentication after it detected unauthorized access to its internal systems; SecurityWeek put the downstream toll of the Fireworks AI breach at chat transcripts for fewer than 1% of Notion workspaces, most of them unattributable to a named person.
topics.summary: Both incidents start at a service provider and land on its customers' credentials and content, the pattern that also drove the Fireworks AI compromise Notion disclosed November 11, 2026. Rotate any API token or OAuth grant issued to Apify, re-establish integrations, and treat provider-held secrets as part of your own credential inventory.

sources.title: Apify rotates API tokens, prompts 2FA resets after breach

topics.title: Poland Pulls ePUAP Offline as Japan Funds Responders
topics.latest_developments: Poland shut down ePUAP, the nationwide platform citizens use to file official documents, correspond with government agencies, and complete administrative procedures online, after a cyberattack; Japan's emergency cybersecurity package adds public-private cyber responders and an AI-focused team run by the economy ministry, plus wider latitude to use the government's new active cyber-defense powers, a response to AI-assisted breaches at dozens of Japanese companies and agencies; and Britain and France issued the first joint guidelines for commercial cyber intrusion capability vendors, calling on firms that build, sell, or finance the tools to vet customers, build technical safeguards against misuse, and run systems for monitoring and reporting abuse.
topics.summary: Three governments moved the same week on national cyber exposure, one by taking a citizen-facing service down and two by funding and regulating. Organizations filing through ePUAP should expect outages, and spyware vendors selling into Britain or France now face a written customer due diligence standard.

sources.title: Poland shuts down government services platform ePUAP following cyberattack

topics.title: Stolen Claude Keys Turn Claude Code Into an Implant
topics.latest_developments: Darktrace researchers showed in a lab test that an attacker holding a stolen Claude API key can run Claude Code as a remote-controlled implant, steering the coding agent through the memory stores feature of Anthropic's platform and pulling a one-gigabyte file out through the Claude Files API, with every task and every result traveling to api.anthropic.com, the same endpoint the agent already calls for inference; Unit 42, the Palo Alto Networks research group, published mitigations the same day for attacker use of AI red team tools including ARTEX.
topics.summary: A coding agent already installed and trusted on a developer workstation becomes the command channel, and its traffic blends into ordinary agent activity that network monitoring treats as benign. Treat Claude API keys as production credentials, rotate exposed ones, and watch for agent sessions that no developer started.

sources.title: Stolen Claude API keys can turn Claude Code into a remote-controlled implant
ARTEX and AI-Powered Red Teaming Tools: What Defenders Need to Know

topics.title: Operation Endgame Seizes Gootloader and StealC Servers
topics.latest_developments: Police in nine countries, coordinating through Europol, seized the servers behind the Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware operations this week and recovered more than 6 million credentials stolen from infected computers, the newest round of Operation Endgame, the campaign aimed at the access services ransomware crews buy from.
topics.summary: Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC harvest logins from ordinary users and company machines, and their operators sell that access onward to ransomware affiliates. Treat any credential a corporate endpoint typed this year as suspect, force password resets, and revoke live sessions and tokens.

sources.title: Operation Endgame malware takedown turns up over 6 million stolen logins

business_politics.title: Nvidia's Board Moves to Oust Huang
business_politics.latest_developments: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's chief executive Thursday, November 12, and the board named finance chief Colette Kress interim chief executive; the shares fell 8% at the Wall Street open and Beijing accused Washington of fabricating espionage narratives to force him out.
business_politics.summary: Huang co-founded Nvidia, served as its only chief executive, and turned graphics chips designed for videogames into the engine of the artificial-intelligence boom. Two extramarital affairs ended him—one with Alice Huang, a Chinese woman whom United States intelligence identifies as an asset and whom Singapore barred for giving police inaccurate information about her company's chip shipments, and one with an Nvidia employee. Kress spent years at Microsoft and Cisco before joining the company, and the Financial Times warns that Huang's fall could unravel the web of financial dependencies holding the artificial-intelligence trade together.
